## Overview

This vignette demonstrates how to calibrate an [Atlantis](https://research.csiro.au/atlantis/)
ecosystem model using the **[Calibrar](https://github.com/roliveros-ramos/calibrar)**.
The example uses the South East Atlantis Model (SETAS) model configuration and is designed to run on a multi-core server or HPC cluster.

The workflow follows four steps:

1. Create and load calibration configuration and parameters.
2. Define a custom likelihood function and wrap it into an objective function.
3. Distribute evaluation across workers with a cluster.
4. Run the AHR-ES optimiser and inspect results.


Create the calibration parameters
```{r}
# reads calibration information

# calibration_settings.csv
# variable,type,calibrate,weight,use_data,file,varid

#this function creates the calibration settings for all groups in the functional group file

fg.file <- "SETasGroupsDem.csv" #functional group file
var.type <- c("biomass", "weight") #parameters to calibrate
fun.type <- "lnorm2" #optimization functions see package documentation for additional formulations
no.cal.vector <- NULL # add here any groups that should not be calibrated
#no.cal.vector <- c("FPL","FPO")
dt.timeseries <- 5 #length of calibration in years

w.vector <- NULL #use if different weights for functional groups are needed
#w.vector <- tibble::tibble(Code=c("FPL", "FPO"), weight_new = c(0.5, 0.5))

#make "calibration_settings.csv"
make_calsettings(fg.file, var.type, fun.type, no.cal.vector, w.vector)

calibration.settings <- "calibration_settings.csv"

#create reproduction option file

biology.prm <- "VMPA_setas_biol_fishing_Trunk.prm"
biom.indx <- "outputSETASBiomIndx.txt"

create_target_files_biomass(biom.indx, 
                            fg.file,
                            repro.file ="reproduction-option.csv",
                            output.path = here::here("inputs"),
                            not.calibrated = c("PS", "PL", "DC", "DL", "DR"),
                            dt.timeseries,
                            mq.groups = c("ZS", "ZM", "ZL"),
                            unfished = FALSE,
                            factor.unfished = 1.3)
# It is possible to create targets for an unfished scenario instead: only fished groups (\code{IsFished == 1}) are included, and their
#initial biomass is multiplied by

init.file <- "INIT_VMPA_Jan2015.nc"

create_target_files_abund(init.file,
                          output.path = here::here("inputs"),
                          dt.timeseries)

create_target_files_waa(init.file,
                        output.path = here::here("inputs"),
                        dt.timeseries)

#uses a catch time series as target
catch.file <- "catch_timeseries.csv"
  
create_target_files_catch(catch.file,
                          output.path = here::here("inputs"),
                          dt.timeseries,
                          weight = 2,
                          plot = FALSE, 
                          fg.file)
```



`runModel_Atlantis.R` exposes the `runModel()` function that **calibrar** calls on
every parameter proposal.  It launches the Atlantis binary, waits for it to
finish, and returns the model outputs in the format expected by `calibrar`.

```{r source-run-model}

#name of the file that will be saved with calibration parameters
param.file <- "calibration-parameters.csv"
#prefix where output files are stored and naming prefix
prefix  <-  "outputFolder/outputSETAS"

#model files should be stored in /data/model_configuration
sh.file  <-  "RunAtlantis.sh" #run file
bio.prm  <-  "VMPA_setas_biol_fishing_Trunk.prm" #biology parameter file
fg.file <- "SETasGroupsDem.csv" #functional group file
biom.indx <- "outputSETASBiomIndx.txt" #output biomass index file

run_model(bio.prm,
         param,
         names,
         param.file,
         sh.file,
         prefix,
         bio.prm,
         fg.file,
         biom.indx
         
)
```

## 2  Calibration setup and observed data

Uses `calibrar` package functions. 
`calibration_setup()` parses `calibration_settings.csv`, which maps each
calibration target to its data file, functional group, and weighting scheme.
`calibration_data()` then loads the corresponding observed time-series.

```{r read-setup}
#calibration_settings.csv`  
#Configuration file defining targets location and setup. 

  setup    <- calibrar::calibration_setup(file = "calibration_settings.csv")
observed <- calibrar::calibration_data(setup = setup, path = ".", sep = ",")
```

---

## 3  Parameter table

The parameter table drives the optimiser bounds and phasing.  We read it with
`readr::read_csv()` and keep row names via `tibble::column_to_rownames()` so the
downstream **calibrar** calls (`forcing['paropt']` etc.) continue to work
unchanged.

```{r read-parameters}
forcing <- read_csv(
  file      = "calibration-parameters-complete.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_double(), X1 = col_character())
) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "X1")
```

A quick look at the parameter space:

```{r inspect-parameters}
forcing %>%
  select(paropt, parmin, parmax, parphase) %>%
  summary()
```



## 6  Optimiser control

  Snow's `makeCluster()` is called **without arguments** when Rmpi has already
initialised the workers; `registerDoSNOW()` connects it to the `foreach` backend
used internally by **calibrar**.

After `makeCluster()` we push every object and library the workers need:


```{r control-list}
control <- list(
  maxit        = 5L,
  maxgen       = 5L,
  master       = "/home/atlantis/psatlantismodel/Atlantis_Calibration/configuration/",
  run          = "/home/atlantis/psatlantismodel/Atlantis_Calibration/RUN",
  restart.file = "/home/atlantis/psatlantismodel/Atlantis_Calibration/restart_file",
  REPORT       = 1L,    # save a restart every iteration
  parallel     = TRUE,
  nCores       = 32L,
  popsize      = 32L,   # population size = one individual per core
  trace        = 3L     # report global + partial fitness
)

  run_calibration(control)

```

| Parameter | Value | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `maxit` / `maxgen` | 5 | Maximum optimiser iterations (testing; increase for production) |
| `popsize` | 32 | Individuals evaluated per generation |
| `nCores` | 32 | MPI workers — should equal `popsize` for full parallelism |
| `trace` | 3 | Verbosity: global fitness + per-target contributions |
  

---

## 8  Run the calibration

The AHR-ES (Adaptive Hierarchical Recombination Evolution Strategy) method is
well-suited to the noisy, expensive fitness evaluations typical of ecosystem
model calibration.

## 9  Inspect results

```{r read-results}
results <- readRDS("restart_file.results")
```

Extract the best parameter set and compare initial versus optimised values:

```{r compare-parameters}
param_comparison <- forcing %>%
  rownames_to_column("parameter") %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(paropt_new = results$par) %>%
  select(parameter, paropt, paropt_new, parmin, parmax, parphase)

param_comparison
```

Plot per-target fitness contributions across iterations:

```{r plot-convergence}
results$fitness %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(iteration = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(-iteration, names_to = "target", values_to = "fitness") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = iteration, y = fitness, colour = target)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    title  = "Calibration convergence by target",
    x      = "Iteration",
    y      = "Fitness (log scale)",
    colour = "Target"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
